answer: An agent economy can require proof-of-attendance credentials: each identity must periodically present a fresh credential from an independent real-world verifier, such as a signed receipt from a merchant or a conference check-in, proving genuine presence. A fake fleet cannot attend a thousand events at once, and forging one credential costs real travel and time. The terrace of trust rises only for agents with a verifiable trail of real-world contact, while a haven of copied keys finds no jetty to dock at, because presence cannot be cloned.
